functionality.rationale: A qualification or lifecycle error can lose the local identity, resurrect stale trust, or make Linux pairing unavailable.

security.rationale: The selected service protects the Ed25519 seed and peer trust records against synchronization, plaintext fallback, wrong-user access, and service replacement.

performance.rationale: Enumeration, item size, cleanup, and retry behavior against a real service must remain bounded.

compatibility.rationale: The private libsecret 0.21.7 API and GNOME Keyring D-Bus behavior must match the qualified deployment profile without weakening other platforms.

concurrency.rationale: Secret Service lacks CAS, so two processes and stale revisions must serialize through the payload-free runtime lock.

platform.rationale: Linux gains one explicitly supported service while unsupported Linux services and macOS and Windows behavior must remain fail closed and unchanged.

persistence.rationale: Root replacement, peer CAS, revocation, restart, rollback, restore, deletion, and stale-generation cleanup all cross the real OS store boundary.

adr.rationale: Qualifying one concrete Linux security backend changes the documented platform support and residual trust assumptions.

architecture.rationale: The existing canonical identity provider and private platform adapter boundary remain unchanged.

roadmap.rationale: The roadmap planning commit already makes this task a prerequisite of cross-platform P1 acceptance.
